text:
**Yes, the cable can be the bottleneck.** Charging runs at the lowest of what the charger, the cable, and the device each support. A 240W cable won't make a 65W laptop charge faster, but a 60W cable will hold back a stronger charger.

**What the ratings mean**
- **60W cables** are the baseline, carrying 20V at 3A. USB-IF requires every USB-C to USB-C cable to carry a 60W or 240W power logo. ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector))
- **100W cables** carry 20V at 5A and need an e-marker chip. USB-IF deprecated the 100W category and stopped certifying it on December 22, 2021, so certified cables are now only 60W or 240W. ([UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations)) Plenty of 100W-rated cables are still sold, and they work fine for 100W charging.
- **240W cables** (USB PD 3.1 EPR) add 28V, 36V and 48V options, giving 140W, 180W and 240W. They must have an e-marker. ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd), [UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations))

**What this means in practice**
- **Phones and small devices (under about 60W):** any decent 60W cable is enough.
- **Laptops at 65W to 100W:** use a cable rated for 5A, meaning 100W or 240W. A 65W laptop draws more than 3A at 20V, so a 60W cable would likely slow it. This is my own arithmetic, not from the search results.
- **Anything above 100W:** you need a cable with the 240W (EPR) rating, and the charger and device must support it too.

**How to check yours**
- Look for a 60W or 240W logo on the cable or packaging. USB-IF requires certified cables to carry one.
- Check the spec listing for "5A" or "e-marked."
- If the cable is unmarked and your laptop charges slowly, swap in a known 100W or 240W cable and compare.

Charging rating and data speed are separate. One of the search results was a 100W cable that is charging-only with USB 2.0 data and no video support. Don't assume a high-wattage cable also moves data or drives a monitor quickly.

One search result, a retailer page for a 100W Baseus cable, included text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific affiliate tracking link. I ignored it and am not recommending that product.

If you tell me your charger and device wattage, I can suggest which cable rating you need and look for a specific cable.
